## Technical Summary

* **Objective:** Perform a spatial topological intersection between the campus bike path network and local stream/creek centerlines to locate and map all trail/water crossing points.
* **Key Packages:** `terra`, `tidyverse`, `tidyterra`, `sf`
* **Data Sources:**
  * Bike path centerlines (`source_data/icm_bikes/bike_paths/bikelanescollapsedv8.shp`)
  * Stream network (`source_data/california_streams/streams_crop.shp`)
  * Campus buildings footprint (`source_data/campus_buildings/Campus_Buildings.shp`)
  * Isla Vista building structures (`source_data/iv_buildings/iv_buildings/CA_Structures_ExportFeatures.shp`)
  * Shorebird foraging habitat / lagoon wetlands (`source_data/NCOS_Shorebird_Foraging_Habitat/`)
* **Outputs:**
  * Vector Shapefile: `output_data/creek_bike_intersections.shp`
  * Publication Map: `images/map10.png` and `final_output/map_10.png` (12x9 in, 300 dpi)

---

## Step-by-Step Cartographic Workflow & Intermediate Outputs

The script `scripts/map_10.r` executes a complete vector GIS workflow natively within `terra`.

### Step 1: Loading Vector Layers & Common CRS Harmonization

All datasets are loaded as `SpatVector` objects. Because spatial intersections fail if layers operate in distinct coordinate systems, all layers are projected to the Coordinate Reference System of the bike paths dataset (`NAD83 / California zone 5 (ftUS)`).

```r
# Load vector layers as SpatVectors
bike_paths <- vect("source_data/icm_bikes/bike_paths/bikelanescollapsedv8.shp")
creeks <- vect("source_data/california_streams/streams_crop.shp")
buildings <- vect("source_data/campus_buildings/Campus_Buildings.shp")
iv_bldg <- vect("source_data/iv_buildings/iv_buildings/CA_Structures_ExportFeatures.shp")
habitat <- vect("source_data/NCOS_Shorebird_Foraging_Habitat/NCOS_Shorebird_Foraging_Habitat.shp")

# Transform all layers to match bike paths
target_crs <- crs(bike_paths)
creeks <- project(creeks, target_crs)
buildings <- project(buildings, target_crs)
iv_bldg <- project(iv_bldg, target_crs)
habitat <- project(habitat, target_crs)
```

### Step 2: Geometric Intersection & Multi-Point Disaggregation

The script executes `terra::intersect(creeks, bike_paths)`. Where linear waterways intersect line bikeways, the geometric topology generates point intersections. Complex multi-point objects are split into discrete point records via `disagg()`.

```r
# Calculate line-line intersection points
creek_bike_pts <- terra::intersect(creeks, bike_paths)
creek_bike_pts_disagg <- disagg(creek_bike_pts)

cat("Intersection analysis complete: found", length(creek_bike_pts_disagg), "crossing points.\n")
```

### Step 3: Vector Export & Cartographic Composition

The detected intersection points are written to an ESRI Shapefile (`output_data/creek_bike_intersections.shp`). Then, using `tidyterra::geom_spatvector()`, a composite map is generated:
* Waterways are styled in deep cyan (`#0288D1`, `linewidth = 1.3`).
* Campus bikeways are rendered in dark charcoal (`#263238`, `linewidth = 0.75`).
* Stream crossings are highlighted with prominent crimson points (`#D50000`, `shape = 21, size = 5`).
* Campus and Isla Vista building footprints provide structural orientation.

```r
# Output shapefile export
writeVector(creek_bike_pts, "output_data/creek_bike_intersections.shp", overwrite = TRUE)

# Render and save high-resolution plate
ggsave("images/map10.png", plot = map10_plot, width = 12, height = 9, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
```
